pro_evidence.argument: Primary endpoint is a strict composite requiring BOTH MASH resolution (CRN ballooning 0, inflammation 0-1) AND fibrosis improvement (>=1 stage decrease) at Week 72, read centrally — the same reading paradigm used at screening (C04), which reduces reader-discordance noise between baseline and endpoint.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: pan-PPAR alpha/delta/gamma agonism simultaneously targets steatohepatitis activity (inflammation/ballooning) and fibrogenesis, so a composite that demands both is mechanistically aligned with the drug's multi-pathway pharmacology rather than a single-pathway bet.

pro_evidence.argument: In the Phase 2b NATIVE trial the 1200 mg dose met the primary endpoint with a statistically significant separation from placebo (55% vs 33%, P=0.007), establishing prior proof of histological activity for the high dose.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: Dose-dependent PPAR engagement: the 1200 mg/day exposure achieved in Phase 2b is carried forward unchanged into NATiV3, so the biological effect size observed at that exposure is the relevant prior for the Phase 3 high-dose arm.

pro_evidence.argument: NATIVE reported the exact component and composite histology rates that map onto the Phase 3 CRN composite (resolution 49%/39% vs 22%; fibrosis improvement 48%/34% vs 29%; composite 35%/25% vs 9%), giving a direct within-drug anchor for the Phase 3 endpoint definition.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: The composite (resolution + fibrosis improvement) is the most demanding and least placebo-prone component; the large NATIVE composite separation (35%/25% vs 9%) indicates the drug's effect is concentrated in the co-occurrence of both histological improvements, which is precisely what the Phase 3 primary tests.

pro_evidence.argument: ESSENCE, a same-construct Phase 3 in F2/F3 MASH with a 72-week CRN composite endpoint, achieved a 32.7% vs 16.1% composite rate (delta 16.5 pp, P<0.001), demonstrating that a 72-week CRN composite is a viable and achievable Phase 3 endpoint in this population.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: Confirms the endpoint is not intrinsically unattainable at 72 weeks in F2/F3; the trial's operating characteristics (power, event rates) are therefore not the binding constraint — drug effect is.

pro_evidence.argument: Enrollment exceeded target (1009 main + 410 exploratory vs 969/350), and the financing covenant required a drop-out rate below 30% before Week 72, with the covenant already satisfied as of 2025-04-01.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: Over-enrollment plus a contractual dropout ceiling increases evaluable biopsy count at Week 72, which directly protects power and reduces the influence of missing-biopsy imputation on the composite endpoint.

pro_evidence.argument: Sample size was sized for 90% power and randomization was stratified by fibrosis stage and diabetic status, matching the stratification factors used in the assumed CMH test.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: Stratification on the two strongest prognostic covariates (fibrosis stage, diabetes) removes between-arm imbalance in the baseline risk of the composite event, tightening the variance of the treatment contrast.

pro_evidence.argument: Last patient last visit occurred in 2026-09 and topline is expected in Q4 2026, so the outcome is physically fixed and unblinded only at the prespecified analysis.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: A locked database removes the possibility of post-hoc endpoint redefinition or cohort trimming, making the readout a clean test of the prespecified composite.

pro_evidence.argument: In NATIVE, adverse-event dropout was under 5% and similar across arms, indicating the safety profile is unlikely to differentially erode the active arms over a longer 72-week exposure.
pro_evidence.mechanism_link: Low and balanced AE-driven discontinuation preserves randomized comparability and limits differential missingness on the biopsy endpoint.

con_evidence.argument: Patients may initiate a GLP-1 receptor agonist after randomization, which introduces an asymmetric post-randomization confounder because placebo-arm patients have greater incentive to add an active weight-loss agent.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: GLP-1 RAs independently improve steatohepatitis and fibrosis; differential drop-in on placebo compresses the placebo-vs-lanifibranor contrast and biases the composite toward the null.

con_evidence.argument: Baseline GLP-1 use was approximately 14% and T2D approximately 55% in the NATiV3 main cohort, so a substantial fraction of the population is already on background incretin or antidiabetic therapy at entry.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: High background GLP-1/SGLT2 use raises the placebo response floor and reduces the incremental histological benefit attributable to lanifibranor, shrinking the observable delta.

con_evidence.argument: Pooled noncirrhotic MASH placebo MASH-resolution rate is 11% (95% CI 8-14%) across 127 studies, but ESSENCE reported a 34.3% placebo resolution rate, showing extreme between-trial variability in the placebo arm.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: Unstable placebo event rates make the assumed control rate a major source of power uncertainty; if NATiV3's placebo behaves like ESSENCE rather than the pooled estimate, the detectable delta shrinks materially.

con_evidence.argument: In NATIVE the 800 mg dose did not reach the primary endpoint (48% vs 33%, P=0.07), so only one of the two Phase 3 doses has prior Phase 2b statistical support.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: If the Phase 3 effect is dose-dependent and the 800 mg arm is underpowered or sub-efficacious, the trial's success hinges on the 1200 mg arm alone, reducing the effective number of independent shots on goal.

con_evidence.argument: NATIVE's composite rate was 35%/25% vs 9% under the SAF reading paradigm, whereas NATiV3 uses the CRN paradigm; the crosswalk between SAF and CRN scoring is not established in the ledger.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: A paradigm shift in histological scoring can change both the active and placebo event definitions, so the Phase 2b composite anchor may not transfer quantitatively to the Phase 3 CRN composite.

con_evidence.argument: Elafibranor, a PPAR agonist in the same mechanistic class, failed its Phase 3 RESOLVE-IT NASH primary endpoint, with no peer-reviewed primary results publication available.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: Class-level Phase 3 failure is a qualitative warning that PPAR-mediated histological improvement in Phase 2 may not replicate at Phase 3 scale, independent of the specific molecule.

con_evidence.argument: ClinicalTrials.gov lists primaryCompletionDate as 2027-09-30 (estimated), reflecting the 48-week Part B/ATE extension, which is later than the company's Q4 2026 topline for Part A.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: The discrepancy signals that the registrational package depends on Part B follow-up beyond the Part A readout, so a positive Part A composite alone may not be sufficient for the intended filing pathway.

con_evidence.argument: The intended filing strategy is FDA Accelerated Approval and EMA Conditional Approval, explicitly subject to positive Phase 3 histology results.
con_evidence.mechanism_link: Accelerated/conditional pathways imply the histology endpoint is a surrogate; even a statistically positive composite may face regulatory scrutiny on clinical benefit, adding non-statistical risk after the readout.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: primary_endpoint_definition (composite: MASH resolution AND fibrosis improvement, Week 72, CRN, central reading)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Defines the event; a stricter composite lowers the expected event rate in both arms relative to single-component endpoints.
Three-arm design with shared placebo; supports Hochberg-style two-dose testing and any-dose decision rule.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: population_definition (SAF A3/A4 + F2/F3, central reading; GLP-1/SGLT2 stable >=3 months; weight stable >=6 months)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Enriched for active steatohepatitis and F2/F3 fibrosis, which raises event rates relative to an all-comers MASH population.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: sample_size_and_dropout (main cohort 1009 vs target 969; dropout covenant <30% before Week 72)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Over-enrollment and a satisfied dropout ceiling increase evaluable N and protect power.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: power_and_stratification (90% power; stratified by fibrosis stage and diabetic status)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Higher power target and stratification on prognostic factors tighten the treatment contrast and reduce variance.
Asymmetric drop-in on placebo compresses the active-vs-placebo delta toward the null.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: phase2b_effect_size_anchor (placebo-adjusted differences: fibrosis 18%, composite 24%, F2/F3 composite 26%)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Company-reported Phase 2b deltas set the prior center for the Phase 3 effect size; these are differences, not response rates.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: phase2b_primary_endpoint_result (1200 mg 55% vs 33%, P=0.007; 800 mg 48% vs 33%, P=0.07 NS)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Supports a positive prior for the 1200 mg dose and a weaker/uncertain prior for the 800 mg dose.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: phase2b_component_and_composite_rates (resolution 49%/39% vs 22%; fibrosis 48%/34% vs 29%; composite 35%/25% vs 9%)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Provides within-drug component and composite anchors; the composite shows the largest separation and the lowest placebo rate.
Low and balanced AE dropout limits differential missingness and preserves randomized comparability.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: external_crn_component_benchmark (MAESTRO-NASH 52-week CRN: resolution 25.9%/29.9% vs 9.7%; fibrosis improvement 24.2%/25.9% vs 14.2%)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Sets an external CRN component benchmark; composite not directly reported, so it informs component-level expectations only.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: external_phase3_composite_benchmark (ESSENCE 72-week CRN composite 32.7% vs 16.1%, delta 16.5 pp, P<0.001)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Demonstrates a 72-week CRN composite is achievable in F2/F3; provides an external active and placebo composite anchor.
Sets a low pooled placebo resolution prior, but the wide between-trial variability (ESSENCE 34.3%) makes the control rate a major uncertainty.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: class_failure_precedent (elafibranor RESOLVE-IT Phase 3 NASH failure, no peer-reviewed primary results)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Qualitative downward pressure on the prior for PPAR-class Phase 3 replication; not used numerically.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: regulatory_pathway (FDA Accelerated Approval / EMA Conditional Approval, subject to positive Phase 3 histology)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Frames histology as a surrogate endpoint; positive statistics do not automatically translate to approval.

evidence_to_parameter_mapping.parameter: primary_completion_date (2027-09-30 estimated, includes Part B ATE 48 weeks)
evidence_to_parameter_mapping.qualitative_direction: Indicates the registrational timeline extends beyond the Part A topline, adding follow-up dependence.
High background GLP-1/T2D prevalence raises the placebo floor and may attenuate the incremental lanifibranor effect; F2/F3 mix affects expected event rates.

gaps.topic: Statistical analysis plan (SAP) not public: alpha, multiplicity procedure, interim alpha spending, test statistic, estimand, and missing-biopsy imputation are all assumed in the design card.
gaps.why_it_matters: The success criterion (alpha, Hochberg vs fixed sequence, ITT vs per-protocol, NRI vs MI) directly determines the probability of a statistically positive readout and cannot be verified from the ledger.
gaps.suggested_source: Inventiva SAP or statistical section of the ClinicalTrials.gov record / regulatory filing; company disclosure of multiplicity and imputation conventions.

gaps.topic: No efficacy interim analysis evidence; all five DMC reviews were safety-only.
gaps.why_it_matters: Absence of an efficacy interim means the full alpha is spent at the final analysis, but also that no early stopping for futility or efficacy is available; this affects the timing and interpretation of the Q4 2026 topline.
gaps.suggested_source: DMC charter or company disclosure confirming no efficacy interim and the final analysis timing.

gaps.topic: SAF-to-CRN histological scoring crosswalk between NATIVE (Phase 2b) and NATiV3 (Phase 3).
gaps.why_it_matters: The Phase 2b effect-size anchor (C09, C11) is expressed under SAF, while the Phase 3 primary uses CRN; without a validated crosswalk the prior center for the Phase 3 composite is uncertain.
gaps.suggested_source: Published methodological comparison of SAF and NASH CRN scoring, or central-reader concordance data from the sponsor.

gaps.topic: Magnitude and differentiality of post-randomization GLP-1 drop-in (C08) in the NATiV3 population.
gaps.why_it_matters: Asymmetric drop-in on placebo is a plausible mechanism for null bias; the size of the effect on the composite endpoint is unknown and not quantified in the ledger.
gaps.suggested_source: Post-hoc or sensitivity analyses of concomitant GLP-1 use by arm; company disclosure of drop-in rates during the trial.

gaps.topic: Actual Week 72 biopsy evaluability and missing-biopsy rate.
gaps.why_it_matters: The composite endpoint requires paired baseline and Week 72 biopsies; the dropout covenant (<30%) is a financing condition, not a biopsy-completion rate, and missing biopsies drive the imputation assumption.
gaps.suggested_source: Company disclosure of biopsy completion rates or the final analysis dataset; regulatory review documents.

gaps.topic: Elafibranor RESOLVE-IT Phase 3 NASH failure has no peer-reviewed primary results publication (C16, tier C).
gaps.why_it_matters: Class-level failure is a qualitative prior input; without a primary publication the mechanism of failure (efficacy vs safety vs population) cannot be assessed for relevance to lanifibranor.
gaps.suggested_source: Genfit regulatory filings, conference abstracts, or FDA/EMA review documents for elafibranor in NASH.

gaps.topic: N=664 blinded pooled histology analysis (C17, tier D) has no located primary source.
gaps.why_it_matters: If real, it could inform the blinded event-rate prior; as unverified it cannot enter the model and remains a future-work item.
gaps.suggested_source: Company PR/deck archive or conference presentation explicitly reporting the N=664 blinded pooled analysis.

gaps.topic: Discrepancy between company topline (Q4 2026, Part A) and ClinicalTrials.gov primaryCompletionDate (2027-09-30, includes Part B ATE).
gaps.why_it_matters: The registrational package may depend on Part B follow-up; the timing and content of the topline relative to the full primary completion affects interpretation of the readout.
gaps.suggested_source: Company clarification of Part A vs Part B reporting, and the ClinicalTrials.gov record's outcome measure time frames.

llm_prior_suggestion.rationale: Advisory only, not entering the model. Anchored on the ledger's within-drug Phase 2b composite separation (C11: 35%/25% vs 9%, i.e., 26/16 pp under SAF) and the company-reported Phase 2b composite effect size of 24% (C09), discounted for (i) the SAF-to-CRN paradigm shift (C11 gap), (ii) asymmetric post-randomization GLP-1 drop-in on placebo (C08), (iii) high baseline T2D (~55%) and GLP-1 (~14%) background therapy (C20), and (iv) the external ESSENCE 72-week CRN composite delta of 16.5 pp (C14) as a same-construct Phase 3 benchmark. The range is deliberately wide because the placebo composite rate is highly uncertain (C15 pooled 11% vs ESSENCE 34.3%).
